oneTimers: Berkshire wrote down its Kraft Heinz stake: a $3.76B after-tax impairment is the biggest piece of the quarter's $4.7B of pre-tax equity-method losses.

Investment gains included $1.5B of paper gains on stocks Berkshire still owns and $4.2B realized on sales (after tax) — far below the $23.9B of pre-tax gains a year ago, which is most of why headline profit fell so sharply.
'Other' operating earnings included $877M of foreign-currency losses on non-dollar debt, versus a $446M gain a year ago.
otherDetail: Investment gains of $6,364M — mostly gains on Berkshire's stock portfolio — less $4,745M of equity-method losses, driven by the write-down of the Kraft Heinz stake, and $87M attributable to noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.text: The businesses themselves earned $11.2B after tax, down from $11.6B — insurance underwriting slipped to $2.0B, while manufacturing, service and retailing rose to $3.6B.
takeaways.title: Operating earnings eased 4%

takeaways.text: Net earnings fell from $30.3B to $12.4B mostly because investment gains shrank from $23.9B to $6.4B pre-tax — market moves, not business performance.
takeaways.title: Headline profit is the noisy number

takeaways.text: Cash, equivalents and Treasury Bills reached about $344B at June 30 — Berkshire is still waiting for a big enough deal at the right price. Insurance float was about $174B.
takeaways.title: The cash pile keeps climbing

verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings slipped 4% to $11.2B, and a $3.8B write-down of its Kraft Heinz stake plus much smaller investment gains cut headline profit to $12.4B — down from $30.3B a year ago.
